newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bavaria stands by Bosnian refugee deportations.
newsitem.headline: Bavaria stands by Bosnian refugee deportations.

text.p: Bavaria, which on Wednesday became the first German state to forcibly send a Bosnian refugee back to his war-ravaged homeland, said on Thursday it would order more deportations.
A state interior ministry spokesman said it would stick to its policy of expelling criminals first and then single people of working age from areas of Bosnia it considers safe.

Germany took in some 320,000 refugees from the 3 1/2-year Bosnian war -- more than the rest of the European Union together. But state interior ministers voted last month they could be sent back from the beginning of October.
Many states, heeding calls from humanitarian groups and the United Nations High Commission for Refugees (UNHCR), have agreed not to start deporting refugees at least until after the winter.

Bavaria and Berlin, however, signalled their intention to begin repatriations as soon as possible. The southern state on Wednesday became the first to carry out its pledge, deporting a 29-year old convicted criminal identified only as Salih M. to Sarajevo.
The deportee had been convicted of several crimes during his time in Germany, the interior minstry said.

The mayor of the northern Bosnian city of Tuzla said in Bonn on Wednesday forcible repatriation of thousands of refugees to former Yugoslavia would exacerbate tensions in Bosnia and cause untold suffering.
Selim Beslagic appealed to state governments to reconsider their decision to start the compulsory return of refugees, warning that Bosnia could not cope with a flood of returnees.
